description: Fig. 1 is a two-panel line-drawn process schematic (no micrograph, spectrum or data curve) of air induction melting (AIM) with a flux cover. (a) is a vertical cross-section of the melting unit: a crucible with "MgO/Al2O3 Lining" surrounded by the "Induction coil", containing "Molten Metal" capped by a "Molten Slag (2-4 mm thick)" layer. Dimension arrows on the left give 300 mm overall crucible height and 240 mm melt depth, and 150 mm for the crucible width. Below/right of the crucible a small refractory trough labelled "Tundish" sits above a vertical "Mould" drawn 80 mm wide on a base plate. (b) is a 3-D perspective of the same assembly during top pouring: the crucible is tilted, and molten metal still blanketed by the molten slag layer flows over the lip as a dashed stream into the tundish and then down into the mould, where a grey "Solidified Ingot" is shown building up. Together the panels depict the process sequence — flux-covered melting, then top pouring into split cast iron moulds. No numeric data are plotted; only the geometry annotations above.

observations.observation: Panel (a) labels the crucible wall material as 'MgO/Al2O3 Lining' and shows an 'Induction coil' surrounding it.
Panel (a) labels a slag cover on top of the melt as 'Molten Slag (2-4 mm thick)', i.e. the printed flux-cover thickness range is 2-4 mm.
Dimension arrows in panel (a) are printed as 300 mm (overall crucible height), 240 mm (melt depth) and 150 mm (crucible width).
Panel (a) shows a 'Tundish' trough and a vertical 'Mould' whose printed width is 80 mm.
Panel (b) labels three features: 'Molten Slag', 'Molten Metal' and 'Solidified Ingot', and shows the metal stream passing from the tilted crucible through the tundish into the mould.
The caption states that the figure is a schematic diagram of air induction melting with flux cover, (a) during melting and (b) during pouring.
The citing text states that sound, porosity-free Fe-Al alloy ingots containing 7 wt.% and 9 wt.% Al were successfully produced by this air-induction-melting-with-flux-cover process (Fig. 1).
The citing text states that 30-kg heats of Fe-Al alloys containing 7 wt.% and 9 wt.% Al were prepared by Inductotherm medium-frequency AIM of 50-kg capacity.
The citing text states that the preheated flux contained Al2O3, CaO, MgO and CaF2 and was added after melting the iron charge to provide a protective cover over the melt.
The citing text states that iron was charged into an alumina-lined crucible and the bath was held at 1900 K for a very short time (2 min) to prevent aluminium losses.
The citing text states that the melt was top poured into split cast iron molds, which corresponds to the pouring geometry drawn in panel (b).
The figure contains no plotted data, axes or measured values; all annotations are geometry labels and dimensions.

sample_hints: flux containing Al2O3, CaO, MgO, and CaF2

subfigures.description: Cross-sectional schematic of the induction melting furnace during melting: MgO/Al2O3-lined crucible with induction coil, molten metal bath covered by a 2-4 mm thick molten slag layer, annotated with dimension arrows of 300 mm (crucible height), 240 mm (melt depth) and 150 mm (crucible width); a tundish trough and a vertical 80 mm-wide mould are drawn beside/below as the downstream casting arrangement.

Three-dimensional perspective schematic of the pouring stage: the crucible is tilted so molten metal, still covered by the molten slag layer, flows over the lip (dashed stream lines) through the tundish into the upright mould, where a grey 'Solidified Ingot' is shown accumulating in the mould cavity.
